'''''Alstroemeria aurea''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[family (botany)|family]] Alstroemeriaceae, [[native species|native]] to Chile and Argentina, but naturalised in Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom.<ref name = GRIN>{{GRIN}}</ref> It is also widely cultivated as an ornamental.

==Common names==
Common names include '''yellow alstroemeria''',<ref name = GRIN/> though cultivars have been selected in a range of colours. The name '''Peruvian lily''' is often applied to this and other species of ''Alstroemeria'', despite the fact that most are not native to that country.{{cn|date=October 2024}}

==Description==
Growing to {{convert|1|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|0.5|m|ft|abbr=on}} broad, it is a [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] with brittle, fleshy roots beneath erect stems with narrow leaves. Many orchid-like flowers<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.gardenia.net/plant/alstroemeria-aurea-peruvian-lily | title = ''Alstroemeria aurea'' | website = Gardenia.net | access-date = 23 August 2021}}</ref> in brilliant shades of yellow and orange. appear in early to midsummer. The flowers may be heavily spotted or striped with red or brown. If undisturbed, plants will spread rapidly in benign conditions.<ref name=RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/67996/Alstroemeria-aurea/Details | title = ''Alstroemeria aurea'' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 28 July 2021}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
When cultivated it is one of the [[hardiness (plants)|hardiest]] alstroemerias, surviving temperatures of {{convert|-10|C|F|abbr=on}}. It requires a sheltered spot in sun or part shade.<ref name = RHSPF/>

==Etymology==
The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''aureum'' means "golden".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book | last=Harrison |first=Lorraine | title=RHS Latin for Gardeners | year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley | location=United Kingdom | isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref>
